parsed.elsewhere_quote: If \(g>1\), then \(P'<P\).\n- If \(g=1\), the new entries are \(1\) and \(mn\). Thus \(P'=P\), while exactly two nonunits have been replaced by one, so \(K'=K-1\).
parsed.explanation: The objection correctly refutes the quoted monotonicity claim. However, the preceding case split supplies the valid argument: if \(g>1\), the gcd output itself exceeds 1; if \(g=1\), the other output is \(mn>1\). Thus no legal move outputs two 1s, so the board cannot become all 1s. Together with the separately proved termination and at-most-one argument, L1.1 is established despite the false sentence. Replacing that sentence with the move-output argument repairs the presentation.
